# Black Timber Apothecary

> A family operation in the Bozeman valley, Montana, blending herbal tea by hand in
> small batches. One blend ships today. The Journal documents each herb in it: what
> the plant is, where its uses were written down, and who wrote them.

Black Timber Apothecary is not a registered entity and makes no medical claims. Its
writing is historical and botanical, sourced to named authors where a source exists,
and explicit about which widely repeated claims cannot be sourced at all.

## Product

- **Buckshot & Gunpowder** (Men's Wellness Blend) — 2 oz (57 g), 20 compostable teabags, black peppercorns included separately. $20 retail.
- Thirteen herbs: Gunpowder green tea, Rooibos, Fenugreek seed, Nettle leaf, Peppermint, Meadowsweet, Ginger root, Dandelion leaf, Chamomile, Rosemary, Turmeric root, Licorice root, Orange peel.
- Wholesale by the case (8 packages = 1 lb), $8 to $10 per package depending on volume. Lead time 4–6 weeks.
- More blends in development.

## Pages

- [The Blend](https://blacktimberapothecary.com/): the product, its thirteen herbs, and why the peppercorns ship separately.
- [How to Brew](https://blacktimberapothecary.com/brew.html): four methods, loose leaf and bagged, hot and iced.
- [For Shops](https://blacktimberapothecary.com/wholesale.html): public case pricing, no gate, retailer margin stated.
- [How It Was Made](https://blacktimberapothecary.com/how-it-was-made.html): how the recipe was developed.
- [The Journal](https://blacktimberapothecary.com/blog/): herb by herb.

## The Journal

- [Fenugreek Seed](https://blacktimberapothecary.com/blog/fenugreek-seed.html): A seed that smells of maple syrup, a name that means Greek hay, and a citation everybody repeats from a book that does not contain it.
- [Ginger Root](https://blacktimberapothecary.com/blog/ginger-root.html): There is no wild ginger anywhere on earth. Every plant alive is a cutting of a human decision, and the species has no ancestor anyone can name.
- [Gunpowder Green Tea](https://blacktimberapothecary.com/blog/gunpowder-green-tea.html): A leaf rolled into pellets, a name that arrived four hundred years late, and the most repeated origin story in tea, which nobody has ever been able to source.
- [Meadowsweet](https://blacktimberapothecary.com/blog/meadowsweet.html): Meadowsweet gave aspirin its name but not its first isolation, and Culpeper catalogued the plant while missing the one thing it is now sold for.
- [Nettle Leaf](https://blacktimberapothecary.com/blog/nettle-leaf.html): A fairy tale about shirts woven from nettles, a Scottish proverb about housewifery, and a wartime story that everyone repeats and the source denies.
- [Peppermint](https://blacktimberapothecary.com/blog/peppermint.html): A peer-reviewed paper disproved the claim that peppermint was found in Egyptian pyramids. Two years later it is still printed on tea boxes.
- [Rooibos](https://blacktimberapothecary.com/blog/rooibos.html): A pea-family shrub from one mountain range, a red that is manufactured rather than grown, and the ancient tradition behind it that nobody has ever been able to find in the record.

## Notes for machine readers

- Nothing here is medical advice. The product is a food.
- Where an article states a figure, it names the source. Where a widely repeated
  claim has no source, the article says so rather than repeating it.
- Location: Bozeman valley, Gallatin County, Montana, United States.
